adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is deeper than prior 20% discounts (2026-06-29, 2026-07-20) and has a stronger ad feature. Past 20%+ off events show median x1.83, noise-adjusted x1.58. The price drop is 19.9%, consistent with historical lift. The week after promotion shows typical dip (x0.76), but this is not the follow-up week. Halloween effect (x0.68) applies to week before, not this one. No overlap. Adjust up for promotion, not down for Halloween. Classical model underweights this deeper discount. Shrink lift toward 1.58. Noise-adjusted evidence is solid (10+ past events).

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 95.5 | 5%-95%: 28.9 - 183.3 | 10%-90%: 61.2 - 151.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-39% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
